tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

"""Channel motion-graphics library: brand-consistent HyperFrames templates -> cached .mov/.mp4 clips. Layout (studio/motion/): shared/mc.css, shared/mc.js shared Minecraft-flavoured primitives + helpers (canonical) fonts/ brand fonts copied from Editing Pack/Fonts templates// SOURCES: template.json (manifest), markup.html, template.css, template.js templates//landscape/ GENERATED HyperFrames project (960x540 logical canvas) templates//vertical/ GENERATED HyperFrames project (540x960 logical canvas) cache/-. rendered clips Generated projects are self-contained (HyperFrames forbids ../ asset paths and one root composition per project), so each gets a lib/ copy of shared/ + fonts and a brand.css built from studio/brand/brand.json. `build()` regenerates them; `render()` calls it automatically. Previews render the logical canvas natively at 30fps; full renders supersample x2 to 1920x1080 / 1080x1920 at 60fps. from mcstudio import motion path = motion.render("time_card", {"text": "3 HOURS LATER"}) # alpha ProRes 4444 .mov path = motion.render("title_card", {"title": "DAY 1"}, opaque=True) # opaque .mp4 card CLI (wired as `mcs motion`): list | render --var k=v ... [--vertical] [--preview] [--opaque] [--duration S] | build [names] """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import hashlib import json import os import re import shutil import subprocess import sys import tempfile import time from pathlib import Path from .paths import STUDIO MOTION = STUDIO / "motion" TEMPLATES = MOTION / "templates" SHARED = MOTION / "shared" FONTS = MOTION / "fonts" CACHE = MOTION / "cache" BUILD = MOTION / "_build" # staged copies for duration overrides BRAND_JSON = STUDIO / "brand" / "brand.json" HYPERFRAMES = os.environ.get("MCS_HYPERFRAMES", "hyperframes@0.8.137") GSAP_URL = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js" # Font files (copied from Editing Pack/Fonts into studio/motion/fonts) and their CSS families. FONT_FACES = [ ("MC Ten", "Minecraft Ten.ttf"), ("Luckiest Guy", "Luckiest Guy.ttf"), ("Minecraft", "Minecraft Regular.otf"), ("Minecraft Bold", "Minecraft Bold.otf"), ] # orientation -> (logical canvas, supersample preset for full renders) ORIENTATIONS = { "landscape": ((960, 540), "landscape"), "vertical": ((540, 960), "portrait"), } SOURCE_FILES = ("template.json", "markup.html", "template.css", "template.js") # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- brand def load_brand() -> dict: return json.loads(BRAND_JSON.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) def _brand_lookup(brand: dict, dotted: str): cur = brand for part in dotted.split("."): cur = cur[part] return cur def brand_css(brand: dict | None = None) -> str: brand = brand or load_brand() lines = ["/* GENERATED by mcstudio.motion from studio/brand/brand.json - do not edit. */"] for fam, fname in FONT_FACES: lines.append(f'@font-face {{ font-family: "{fam}"; src: url("fonts/{fname}"); font-display: block; }}') lines.append(":root {") for k, v in brand.get("colors", {}).items(): lines.append(f" --{k}: {v};") lines.append("}") return "\n".join(lines) + "\n" # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- templates def _manifest(name: str) -> dict: p = TEMPLATES / name / "template.json" if not p.exists(): have = ", ".join(t["name"] for t in list_templates()) raise ValueError(f"unknown motion template '{name}' (have: {have})") m = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) m["name"] = name m.setdefault("orientations", list(ORIENTATIONS)) return m def list_templates() -> list[dict]: """All templates with their manifest (name, description, duration, kind, orientations, vars...).""" out = [] if TEMPLATES.exists(): for d in sorted(TEMPLATES.iterdir()): if (d / "template.json").exists(): out.append(_manifest(d.name)) return out _HTML = """ {name} ({orientation})
{markup}
""" def _write_if_changed(p: Path, data: bytes) -> bool: if p.exists() and p.read_bytes() == data: return False p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) p.write_bytes(data) return True def _fmt_num(x: float) -> str: return str(int(x)) if float(x).is_integer() else str(x) def build(name: str) -> list[Path]: """Regenerate templates/// projects. Only touches files whose content changed.""" m = _manifest(name) tdir = TEMPLATES / name brand = load_brand() decl = [] for key, spec in m.get("vars", {}).items(): d = _brand_lookup(brand, spec["brand"]) if "brand" in spec else spec.get("default") decl.append({"id": key, "type": spec.get("type", "string"), "label": spec.get("label", key), "default": d}) decl_s = json.dumps(decl, ensure_ascii=False).replace("'", "'") markup_p = tdir / "markup.html" markup = markup_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip() if markup_p.exists() else "" markup = "\n".join(" " + ln if ln.strip() else ln for ln in markup.splitlines()) css = brand_css(brand).encode("utf-8") out = [] for orientation in m["orientations"]: (w, h), _ = ORIENTATIONS[orientation] pdir = tdir / orientation html = _HTML.format(name=name, decl=decl_s, w=w, h=h, dur=_fmt_num(float(m["duration"])), orientation=orientation, markup=markup, gsap=GSAP_URL) _write_if_changed(pdir / "index.html", html.encode("utf-8")) for f in ("template.css", "template.js"): if (tdir / f).exists(): _write_if_changed(pdir / f, (tdir / f).read_bytes()) for f in SHARED.glob("*"): if f.is_file(): _write_if_changed(pdir / "lib" / f.name, f.read_bytes()) for _, fname in FONT_FACES: _write_if_changed(pdir / "lib" / "fonts" / fname, (FONTS / fname).read_bytes()) _write_if_changed(pdir / "lib" / "brand.css", css) out.append(pdir) return out def _coerce(spec: dict, value): t = spec.get("type", "string") if t == "number": f = float(value) return int(f) if f.is_integer() else f if t == "boolean": if isinstance(value, bool): return value return str(value).strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on") return str(value) def resolve_vars(name: str, vars: dict | None = None) -> dict: """Manifest defaults (brand refs resolved from brand.json) overlaid with caller vars, type-coerced.""" m = _manifest(name) brand = load_brand() specs = m.get("vars", {}) out = {} for key, spec in specs.items(): out[key] = _brand_lookup(brand, spec["brand"]) if "brand" in spec else spec.get("default") for key, val in (vars or {}).items(): if key not in specs: raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' has no var '{key}' (vars: {', '.join(specs)})") out[key] = val return {k: _coerce(specs[k], v) for k, v in out.items()} def _fingerprint(tdir: Path) -> list: files = [tdir / f for f in SOURCE_FILES if (tdir / f).exists()] files += [p for p in sorted(SHARED.glob("*")) if p.is_file()] files += [FONTS / f for _, f in FONT_FACES] + [BRAND_JSON] return [[p.name, p.stat().st_mtime_ns, p.stat().st_size] for p in files] def _npx() -> str: exe = shutil.which("npx") or shutil.which("npx.cmd") if not exe: raise RuntimeError("npx not found on PATH (Node 22+ is required for HyperFrames)") return exe def _stage_duration(pdir: Path, base: float, duration: float, key: str) -> Path: """Copy a built project with root/clip data-duration rewritten (HyperFrames fixes it at compile time).""" dst = BUILD / key if dst.exists(): shutil.rmtree(dst) shutil.copytree(pdir, dst) p = dst / "index.html" html = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") html = html.replace(f'data-duration="{_fmt_num(base)}"', f'data-duration="{_fmt_num(duration)}"') p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8") return dst def render(name: str, vars: dict | None = None, orientation: str = "landscape", preview: bool = False, opaque: bool = False, duration: float | None = None, force: bool = False, verbose: bool = False) -> Path: """Render a template to studio/motion/cache/-. and return the path (cached). orientation: "landscape" (1920x1080) or "vertical" (1080x1920). preview=True -> 960x540/540x960 @30fps. opaque=True -> mp4 on the brand ink background (card segments); default ProRes 4444 .mov with alpha. duration: override length for manifests with "stretchable": true (the hold section grows). The hash covers name + resolved vars + orientation + preview + opaque + duration + source/shared/font file mtimes + brand.json, so edits to a template invalidate its cache. """ if orientation not in ORIENTATIONS: raise ValueError(f"orientation must be one of {list(ORIENTATIONS)}") m = _manifest(name) if orientation not in m["orientations"]: raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' has no {orientation} version") tdir = TEMPLATES / name _, res_preset = ORIENTATIONS[orientation] rv = resolve_vars(name, vars) if "opaque" in m.get("vars", {}): rv["opaque"] = bool(opaque) elif opaque: raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' does not support opaque renders") base_dur = float(m["duration"]) if duration is not None: duration = float(duration) if abs(duration - base_dur) < 1e-6: duration = None elif not m.get("stretchable"): raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' is not stretchable; its duration is fixed at {base_dur}s") elif duration < float(m.get("min_duration", base_dur)): raise ValueError(f"template '{name}' needs at least {m.get('min_duration', base_dur)}s") key_src = json.dumps({ "name": name, "vars": rv, "orientation": orientation, "preview": bool(preview), "opaque": bool(opaque), "duration": duration, "hf": HYPERFRAMES, "files": _fingerprint(tdir), }, sort_keys=True) h = hashlib.sha256(key_src.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12] ext = "mp4" if opaque else "mov" CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) out = CACHE / f"{name}-{h}.{ext}" if out.exists() and out.stat().st_size > 0 and not force: return out build(name) pdir = tdir / orientation proj = pdir if duration is None else _stage_duration(pdir, base_dur, duration, f"{name}-{h}") fd, var_file = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{name}-", suffix=".json", dir=CACHE) with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(rv, f) tmp_out = CACHE / f".{name}-{h}.part.{ext}" cmd = [_npx(), "--yes", HYPERFRAMES, "render", str(proj), "--format", ext, "--fps", "30" if preview else "60", "--variables-file", var_file, "--strict-variables", "-o", str(tmp_out)] if not preview: cmd += ["--resolution", res_preset] if ext == "mp4": cmd += ["--quality", "draft" if preview else "high"] if not verbose: cmd.append("--quiet") t0 = time.time() try: r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=not verbose, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if r.returncode != 0 or not tmp_out.exists() or tmp_out.stat().st_size == 0: tail = ((r.stdout or "") + "\n" + (r.stderr or ""))[-3000:] if not verbose else "" raise RuntimeError(f"hyperframes render failed for '{name}' (exit {r.returncode}):\n{tail}") os.replace(tmp_out, out) finally: for p in (Path(var_file), tmp_out): try: p.unlink() except OSError: pass if proj != pdir: shutil.rmtree(proj, ignore_errors=True) if verbose: print(f"[motion] {name} rendered in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s", file=sys.stderr) return out # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI def _parse_var(s: str) -> tuple[str, str]: if "=" not in s: raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"--var expects k=v, got '{s}'") k, v = s.split("=", 1) return k.strip(), v def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="mcs motion", description="Channel motion-graphics templates (HyperFrames).") sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True) sub.add_parser("list", help="list templates and their vars") rp = sub.add_parser("render", help="render a template (prints the output path)") rp.add_argument("name") rp.add_argument("--var", action="append", default=[], type=_parse_var, metavar="K=V") rp.add_argument("--vertical", action="store_true", help="1080x1920 instead of 1920x1080") rp.add_argument("--preview", action="store_true", help="half resolution, 30fps") rp.add_argument("--opaque", action="store_true", help="opaque mp4 on brand ink (for card segments)") rp.add_argument("--duration", type=float, help="override length (stretchable templates only)") rp.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="ignore the cache") rp.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true") bp = sub.add_parser("build", help="(dev) regenerate the landscape/vertical HyperFrames projects") bp.add_argument("names", nargs="*", help="templates (default: all)") a = ap.parse_args(argv) if a.cmd == "build": for n in a.names or [t["name"] for t in list_templates()]: for p in build(n): print(p) return 0 if a.cmd == "list": for t in list_templates(): extra = f" stretchable>={t.get('min_duration', t['duration'])}s" if t.get("stretchable") else "" print(f"{t['name']:<13} {t['duration']:>5}s [{'+'.join(t['orientations'])}{extra}] {t.get('description', '')}") for k, spec in t.get("vars", {}).items(): if k == "opaque": continue dflt = f"brand:{spec['brand']}" if "brand" in spec else json.dumps(spec.get("default")) print(f" {k:<13} {spec.get('type', 'string'):<8} default {dflt}") return 0 try: p = render(a.name, dict(a.var), orientation="vertical" if a.vertical else "landscape", preview=a.preview, opaque=a.opaque, duration=a.duration, force=a.force, verbose=a.verbose) except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as e: print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr) return 1 print(p) return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

A composition is an HTML file whose DOM declares timing with `data-*` attributes, whose animation runtime is seekable, and whose media playback is owned by the framework. content.content:
# Determinism, Animation Runtime, and Layout HyperFrames seeks compositions frame-by-frame. Every frame must be reproducible from its time value alone — same input time → same pixels. Three contracts enforce this: the **animation runtime contract**, the **determinism rules**, and the **layout contract**. ## Animation Runtime Contract GSAP is the primary runtime. The core requirement is generic: animation state must be seekable from HyperFrames time. For GSAP: - Create the timeline **synchronously** during page initialization. - Use `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })`. - Register it on `window.__timelines[""]`. - The key must match `data-composition-id` on the composition root. - **Do not** call `tl.play()` for render-critical motion. - **Do not** build timelines inside `async`, `Promise`, `setTimeout`, or event handlers — the renderer can sample before they finish. - **Do not** create empty tweens only to set duration; use `data-duration` on the clip instead. - **Do not** `gsap.set()` clip elements from later scenes — they are not in the DOM at page load. Use `tl.set(selector, vars, time)` inside the timeline at or after the clip's `data-start`. Use the `hyperframes-animation` skill for tween syntax, position parameters, eases, and performance rules. ### Duration Contract For Non-GSAP Runtimes The render engine needs a positive total duration before it will capture a single frame — without one, capture fails outright with "Composition has zero duration." A GSAP timeline supplies this automatically. CSS, WAAPI, and Lottie compositions have no timeline object, so the runtime infers duration itself: - **CSS**: longest `animation-delay` + `animation-duration` × finite `animation-iteration-count` across animated elements (offset by each element's `data-start`). `animation-iteration-count: infinite` cannot be inferred. - **WAAPI**: longest `element.animate()` effect's `getComputedTiming().endTime`. Infinite `iterations` cannot be inferred. - **Lottie**: the registered animation's native length (`totalFrames / frameRate`, or the dotLottie player's own `duration`) — always finite regardless of `loop`. - **Three.js**: **not inferable**. The `three` adapter only forwards time via `hf-seek` — it has no `AnimationClip`/`AnimationMixer` inspection. `data-duration` on the root `[data-composition-id]` element is therefore optional whenever every non-GSAP animation on the page is finite (CSS/WAAPI with finite iteration counts, or Lottie). It is **required** when: the composition has an infinite/unbounded CSS or WAAPI animation, the composition uses Three.js, or there is no GSAP timeline and no animation signal at all for any adapter to discover. `npx hyperframes lint` enforces exactly this (`root_composition_missing_duration_source`) — see the runtime/adapter-specific docs under `hyperframes-animation/adapters/` for the full contract per runtime. ## Determinism Rules Rendered frames must be reproducible from the requested time. Do **not** use any of the following for visual state: - `Date.now()`, `performance.now()`, or any render-time clock. - Unseeded `Math.random()`. Use a seeded PRNG if random-looking placement is needed. - Render-time network fetches for required assets. Inline or pre-bundle them. - Hover, scroll, pointer, or focus state. The renderer has no input events. - Infinite loops such as `repeat: -1`. Compute a finite count: `repeat: Math.max(0, Math.floor(duration / cycleDuration) - 1)` — **`floor`, not `ceil`** (`ceil` overshoots `data-duration` and trips the `gsap_repeat_ceil_overshoot` lint; `max(0, …)` avoids a negative repeat = infinite). Also avoid: - Animating anything outside the visual-property allowlist: `opacity`, `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `color`, `backgroundColor`, `borderRadius`, and transforms. Never tween `display` or raw `visibility`. GSAP `autoAlpha` is allowed on a registered seekable timeline because it interpolates opacity and changes visibility only at the hidden endpoint. A zero-duration `tl.set(..., { visibility: "hidden" | "visible" })` is also allowed at an explicit beat boundary for a deterministic hard kill. Both exceptions apply only to non-clip elements or wrappers inside a clip. Never target a `.clip` element: HyperFrames timing owns its lifecycle and visibility. - Animating the same property on the same element from multiple timelines at the same time — GSAP's overwrite behavior is order-dependent and can flip between renders. ## Layout Contract Build the visible end-state in static HTML and CSS first, then animate from/to that state. - The composition root has fixed pixel frame dimensions. - **The root composition's total duration (render length / frame count) is fixed at compile time**, read once from the static root `data-duration` before scripts run, like `data-width` / `data-height`. A script or `--variables` value that rewrites the root `data-duration` afterward is ignored. To vary render length per output, author the root `data-duration` directly. (A _clip's_ own `data-duration` is re-read from the live DOM, so scripts/variables can still drive clip lengths. Only when the root omits `data-duration` does the renderer probe the live DOM / timeline for total length.) - Scene containers should fill the scene with `width: 100%; height: 100%; box-sizing: border-box`. - Use padding, flex, grid, and `max-width` for layout. Avoid positioning main content with hardcoded `top`/`left` offsets when a layout container can do it. - Use `position: absolute` for layers and decorative elements, not as the default content-layout strategy. - Prefer transforms and opacity for animation. - Keep text inside its intended container. For dynamic text, use `max-width`, wrapping, or `window.__hyperframes.fitTextFontSize(text, { maxWidth, fontFamily, fontWeight })`. - For text measurement without DOM reflow, use `window.__hyperframes.pretext`. Measure off a canvas instead of writing into the page and reading it back, so nothing reflows: `pretext.prepare(text, font)` then `pretext.layout(prepared, maxWidth, lineHeight)` → `{ lineCount, height }`. `prepare` does the font measurement; everything downstream of a prepared string is arithmetic and cheap enough to run per frame. `fitTextFontSize` is built on it. - `layout` gives you height, not width. To size a container to its text (shrinkwrap), use `pretext.prepareWithSegments(text, font)` and then `pretext.measureNaturalWidth(prepared)` for the single-line width, or `pretext.measureLineStats(prepared, maxWidth)` for `{ lineCount, maxLineWidth }`. - `font` is a CSS font shorthand string, e.g. `"700 90px Inter"`. - `clearCache` and `setLocale` are deliberately not exposed: they mutate state shared across compositions, which would make a render depend on what ran before it. - **Do not** use `
` in body text. Forced breaks ignore the actual rendered font width and produce an extra break when the line already wraps naturally, causing overlap. Let text wrap via `max-width`. Exception: short display titles where each word is deliberately on its own line. - **Transformed elements must be block-level + sized.** `transform`/`scaleX`/`scaleY` is a no-op on an inline ``, and scaling an auto-width (0px) element shows nothing → invisible bars/fills. Give them `display: block`/`inline-block`/flex-item **and** a real `width`/`height` (e.g. `width: 100%` inside a sized parent). _(Silent — automated gates may miss it.)_ - **Absolutely-positioned decoratives that pulse or overshoot** (`yoyo` scale, `back.out`) need clearance at their **peak** size and must not straddle an `overflow: hidden` edge — else they overlap a neighbor or get clipped. Position for the largest frame, not the resting one. _(silent.)_ ## Why This Matters The renderer takes a time value and produces a pixel buffer. There is no notion of "playback" — every frame is a fresh seek. Any state that depends on having reached this frame _through_ a prior frame (timers, accumulated state, event-driven animations) will desync when the renderer samples out of order or in parallel. If you find yourself reaching for `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, or `addEventListener` to drive a visual, rebuild it as a tween on the timeline instead. hyperframes-animation/SKILL.md input.message:
I built all 6 new templates. Each one has landscape and vertical versions, all 12 projects pass `npx hyperframes check` with 0 findings, and I rendered every template in preview mode in both orientations and looked at the extracted frames. Every render is `yuva444p12le` (it has alpha). The overlays and wipes start and end fully transparent (first and last frame alpha max is 0). For both wipes, the alpha minimum is 255 at the cut frame, so the frame really is fully covered there.

| Template | Length | Vars (default) | Cut / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pixel_wipe` | 0.9s | `style` ("color", or stone, dirt, grass, deepslate, obsidian, netherrack, sand), `color` (brand grass), `opaque` | Fully covered **0.37–0.48s**, **`cut_at` 0.42**. 64px blocks with procedural 16x16 Minecraft textures pop in along a noisy diagonal wave, then pop out in a fresh random order. |
| `block_break_wipe` | 1.0s | `style` ("stone", same list), `color` (brand diamond), `opaque` | Fully covered **0.30–0.52s**, **`cut_at` 0.42**. 96px blocks are placed from the centre outwards and 5 break-stage crack textures spread across them. Each block then shatters into 2x2 tumbling pieces (centre first); the last debris is gone by 0.98s. |
| `location_tag` | 3s | `text` ("THE NETHER"), `sub` ("X -142  Y 31  Z 2077", empty = none), `icon` ("portal", or compass, eye, sun, moon, diamond, emerald, gold, heart, skull, pick, or 1–2 characters), `color` (brand amethyst), `opaque` | A pixel-art icon block slams in, an ink panel unfurls, the letters pop and a shine sweeps across. The digits in the coordinates line scramble before settling. It sits in the upper third and exits over the last 0.5s. |
| `countdown` | 4s, **stretchable** (min 2s) | `from` (3, range 1–20), `go_text` ("GO!"), `color` ("" = auto: 3 redstone, 2 gold, 1 diamond), `go_color` (brand grass), `opaque` | Each number is built from beveled 5x7 pixel blocks, with a square frame of 24 ticks lighting clockwise, and the blocks burst away at the end of the number. GO! slams in with a shake and a block burst. |
| `progress_tracker` | 2.5s | `label` ("DIAMONDS"), `from` (3), `to` (4), `total` (10), `icon` ("diamond", same list as `location_tag`, or empty), `accent` (brand diamond), `done_text` ("COMPLETE!"), `opaque` | A GUI panel with a segmented bar (up to 24 segments, proportional above that). The bar fills to `to` at 0.9s with a flash and sparkles, and the count rolls like an odometer. It drains instead if `to < from`. The COMPLETE! stamp appears when `to` reaches `total`. Top-left on landscape, top-centre on vertical. |
| `question_card` | 3.5s | `title` ("WOULD YOU RATHER"), `a`, `b`, `or_text` ("OR"), `a_color` (redstone), `b_color` (diamond), `accent` (gold), `opaque` | A title plate drops in, then the A and B cards fly in from opposite sides with letter tags, an OR block spins in, and each option gets a vote pulse. Cards sit side by side on landscape and stacked on vertical (kept above about 70% of the height). |

**Countdown length:** `motion.py` fixes duration in the manifest, so the countdown can't change its own length from `from`. Pass `duration = from + 1` when rendering, e.g. `M.render('countdown', {'from': 10}, 'vertical', duration=11)`. I tested exactly that call and the two-digit 10 fits. If the duration is shorter than that, the numbers are squeezed rather than broken. `template.json` records this as `duration_rule`.

**Render times (preview, 30fps):**
- Wipes: about 10–11s each.
- The other templates: about 16–24s each.
- `countdown` from 10 at 11s long: about 24s.
- I didn't run any full 60fps renders.

**Things to know:**
- **Docs not updated:** I didn't add these templates to `studio/motion/README.md`, because you limited me to the new template folders. The `cut_at` and `covered` values are in each wipe's `template.json`.
- **Check fixes:** to get 0 findings I marked some intentional mask, slide and shatter overflow with HyperFrames' `data-layout-allow-overflow` / `data-layout-allow-occlusion` attributes. I also slightly darken light option colours in `question_card` so the paper text passes the contrast check.
- **Textures:** both wipes draw their textures with a seeded canvas (`toDataURL`). An SVG version left semi-transparent seams at the "covered" moment, and the canvas version fixed that.
- **Icon code duplicated:** the pixel icon set and the texture helper are copied into each template's own `template.js`, per your no-shared-edits rule.
- **Existing `lower_third` may have the same flaw:** in my panel slide-out, a 1% offset left the panel's drop-shadow visible on the first and last frames, and I fixed mine by using a 4% offset. `lower_third` uses the same pattern, so it may show the same sliver; I didn't touch it.
- **Leftover files:** test renders are in `studio/motion/cache/`, which is safe to delete.

All new files are in `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Minecraft Channel\studio\motion\templates\`, under `pixel_wipe`, `block_break_wipe`, `location_tag`, `countdown`, `progress_tracker` and `question_card`. Each folder has `template.json`, `markup.html`, `template.css` and `template.js`, plus the generated `landscape/` and `vertical/` projects.
